Consumer complaint narrative:
In XXXX of XXXX, I had multiple ( XXXX ) credit card accounts closed by Capital One. The accounts were closed due to multiple returned payments ; however, Capital One had previously, for years, provided an option to pay balances immediately using a debit card. This practice stopped in mid to late XXXX ( XXXX timeframe ). I personally contacted Capital One at this time and was informed that they no longer accepted any other form of payment aside from direct ACH from a checking account, which is not immediate and can take days to process depending on normal business hours and holidays. This change directly resulted in the loss of my ability to immediately pay outstanding debts with the instantaneous debit payment method that I had utilized for YEARS previously, which had resulted in an improved credit rating, and the ability to quickly pay down balances. Since two of the three Capital One cards were my oldest credit card accounts, they supported my credit history as my longest open accounts post-bankruptcy. After XX/XX/XXXX, and no longer being able to pay debts immediately with a debit card due to a change in Capital One policy, scheduled payments were not always processed immediately and at times resulted in a returned payment. As a result of only being allowed to submit ACH payments rather than immediate debit payments, my ability to fulfill these transactions were hindered. Additionally, although some payments were returned ( as they were more than the minimum required payment ), very importantly, I was still never late on any minimum required monthly payment for these cards. 

Regardless, without warning, Capital One abruptly closed all of my credit accounts, hindering my credit score and credit access. Insultingly, their prohibition on debit card payments seemed to have only been enforced during this difficult time from late XXXX until early XXXX, as it now seems that they are accepting debit card payments again. However, their 9 month hiatus directly negatively affected my ability to timely fulfill debt payments, and I was personally negatively affected by the impact of their decision to close my credit accounts, again without warning, after several years of a balanced relationship. 

My chief concern is that my ability to pay a debt immediately, a process that I was accustomed to for years thanks to the flexibility of their cards and debit payment system, was suddenly removed. And almost simultaneously, as all three of my credit accounts were closed by creditor without warning, XXXX of XXXX, the ability to pay via debit card suddenly reappeared. 

At the very least, the closing of the accounts after years of positive history shows a fear by the creditor, although the creditor directly removed the simplest form of payment and debt settlement. Only to months later, after filtering out customers such as myself who were credit challenged and paid religiously via debit card, bring back the simple, accessible payment method that I had used for years prior. 

It seems intentional, and it seems unfair. I would never have defaulted on any payment if it were directly deducted from my debit card, as it had been for years previously. Now, my credit rating has again been impacted, thanks to suddenly having to the door slammed in my face by a company that I once thought was an ally to extend credit to someone who was emerging from bankruptcy. They actually helped me get back on to my feet and re-establish my credit. Except for the fact that 9 years and 6 months in, they suddenly no longer had an interest in my money or business. 

I would appreciate an inquiry and explanation into Capital Ones brief hiatus of debit payments, their abrupt cancellation of extended credit, and the reemergence of the ability to pay via debit card. Im sure that they have covered their rear ends with pages of legalese that protects their rights to do so, but they have unfairly alienated groups of people by prohibiting them from fulfilling making payments in a traditional manner that was well established. 

I look forward to a response CFPB, as well as Capital One. At the very least, I would like my positive credit history and longevity accurately reflected within current credit reports. The unexpected closing of these accounts has severely impacted my length of credit history, and now negatively affects my ability to purchase a home, which was a huge possibility 6 months ago. 

Thank you.

transmitted to an obligor a statement of the obligor 's account in connection with an extension of consumer credit, receives at the address disclosed under section 1637 ( b ) ( 10 ) of this title a written notice ( other than notice on a payment stub or other payment medium supplied by the creditor if the creditor so stipulates with the disclosure required under section 1637 ( a ) ( 7 ) of this title ) from the obligor in which the obligor ( 1 ) sets forth or otherwise enables the creditor to identify the name and account number ( if any ) of the obligor, ( 2 ) indicates the obligor 's belief that the statement contains a billing error and the amount of such billing error, and ( 3 ) sets forth the reasons for the obligor 's belief ( to the extent applicable ) that the statement contains a billing error, the creditor shall, unless the obligor has, after giving such written notice and before the expiration of the time limits herein specified, agreed that the statement was correct ( A ) not later than thirty days after the receipt of the notice, send a written acknowledgment thereof to the obligor, unless the action required in subparagraph ( B ) is taken within such thirty-day period, and ( B ) not later than two complete billing cycles of the creditor ( in no event later than ninety days ) after the receipt of the notice and prior to taking any action to collect the amount, or any part thereof, indicated by the obligor under paragraph ( 2 ) either ( i ) make appropriate corrections in the account of the obligor, including the crediting of any finance charges on amounts erroneously billed, and transmit to the obligor a notification of such corrections and the creditor 's explanation of any change in the amount indicated by the obligor under paragraph ( 2 ) and, if any such change is made and the obligor so requests, copies of documentary evidence of the obligor 's indebtedness ; or ( ii ) send a written explanation or clarification to the obligor, after having conducted an investigation, setting forth to the extent applicable the reasons why the creditor believes the account of the obligor was correctly shown in the statement and, upon request of the obligor, provide copies of documentary evidence of the obligor 's indebtedness. In the case of a billing error where the obligor alleges that the creditor 's billing statement reflects goods not delivered to the obligor or his designee in accordance with the agreement made at the time of the transaction, a creditor may not construe such amount to be correctly shown unless he determines that such goods were actually delivered, mailed, or otherwise sent to the obligor and provides the obligor with a statement of such determination.

After complying with the provisions of this subsection with respect to an alleged billing error, a creditor has no further responsibility under this section if the obligor continues to make substantially the same allegation with respect to such error.

( b ) Billing error For the purpose of this section, a " billing error '' consists of any of the following : ( 1 ) A reflection on a statement of an extension of credit which was not made to the obligor or, if made, was not in the amount reflected on such statement.

( 2 ) A reflection on a statement of an extension of credit for which the obligor requests additional clarification including documentary evidence thereof.

( 3 ) A reflection on a statement of goods or services not accepted by the obligor or his designee or not delivered to the obligor or his designee in accordance with the agreement made at the time of a transaction.

( 4 ) The creditor 's failure to reflect properly on a statement a payment made by the obligor or a credit issued to the obligor.

( 5 ) A computation error or similar error of an accounting nature of the creditor on a statement.

( 6 ) Failure to transmit the statement required under section 1637 ( b ) of this title to the last address of the obligor which has been disclosed to the creditor, unless that address was furnished less than twenty days before the end of the billing cycle for which the statement is required.

( 7 ) Any other error described in regulations of the Bureau.

( c ) Action by creditor to collect amount or any part thereof regarded by obligor to be a billing error For the purposes of this section, " action to collect the amount, or any part thereof, indicated by an obligor under paragraph ( 2 ) '' does not include the sending of statements of account, which may include finance charges on amounts in dispute, to the obligor following written notice from the obligor as specified under subsection ( a ), if ( 1 ) the obligor 's account is not restricted or closed because of the failure of the obligor to pay the amount indicated under paragraph ( 2 ) of subsection ( a ), and ( 2 ) the creditor indicates the payment of such amount is not required pending the creditor 's compliance with this section.

Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit any action by a creditor to collect any amount which has not been indicated by the obligor to contain a billing error.

( d ) Restricting or closing by creditor of account regarded by obligor to contain a billing error Pursuant to regulations of the Bureau, a creditor operating an open end consumer credit plan may not, prior to the sending of the written explanation or clarification required under paragraph ( B ) ( ii ), restrict or close an account with respect to which the obligor has indicated pursuant to subsection ( a ) that he believes such account to contain a billing error solely because of the obligor 's failure to pay the amount indicated to be in error. Nothing in this subsection shall be deemed to prohibit a creditor from applying against the credit limit on the obligor 's account the amount indicated to be in error.

( e ) Effect of noncompliance with requirements by creditor Any creditor who fails to comply with the requirements of this section or section 1666a of this title forfeits any right to collect from the obligor the amount indicated by the obligor under paragraph ( 2 ) of subsection ( a ) of this section, and any finance charges thereon, except that the amount required to be forfeited under this subsection may not exceed {$50.00}.

Regulation of credit reports ( a ) Reports by creditor on obligor 's failure to pay amount regarded as billing error After receiving a notice from an obligor as provided in section 1666 ( a ) of this title, a creditor or his agent may not directly or indirectly threaten to report to any person adversely on the obligor 's credit rating or credit standing because of the obligor 's failure to pay the amount indicated by the obligor under section 1666 ( a ) ( 2 ) of this title, and such amount may not be reported as delinquent to any third party until the creditor has met the requirements of section 1666 of this title and has allowed the obligor the same number of days ( not less than ten ) thereafter to make payment as is provided under the credit agreement with the obligor for the payment of undisputed amounts. 

( b ) Reports by creditor on delinquent amounts in dispute ; notification of obligor of parties notified of delinquency If a creditor receives a further written notice from an obligor that an amount is still in dispute within the time allowed for payment under subsection ( a ) of this section, a creditor may not report to any third party that the amount of the obligor is delinquent because the obligor has failed to pay an amount which he has indicated under section 1666 ( a ) ( 2 ) of this title, unless the creditor also reports that the amount is in dispute and, at the same time, notifies the obligor of the name and address of each party to whom the creditor is reporting information concerning the delinquency.

ates my constitutional right to contract freely without interference.

ddition to their mishandling of the securities and failure to honor my lawful payments, I am concerned that AMERICAN EXPRESS may be engaging in fraudulent activities. has used deceptive or unclear language that ob

scures the nature of my rights and obligations, particularly in regard to the use of lawful money and the nature of the securities provided. Violation of Holder-in-Due-Course Laws : As the holder of the securities and negotiable instruments I tendered, I am entitled to the protections and rights outlined in UCC 3-302. A holder in due course has the right to enforce the payment of the instrument free

nstruments, in violation of UCC 3-305 ( concerning defenses and claims to an instrument ). l money ( postage stamps ), fully satisfied the obligation. UCC 3-305 : Outlines claims and defenses to negotiable instruments, including wrongful retention.

UCC 1-201 ( b ) ( 24 ) : Defines lawful money, including postage stamps affixed to negotiable instruments.

Consumer complaint narrative:
On XX/XX/year> I booked three flights through XXXX for XXXX airline tickets for {$650.00} per ticket for a total of {$1900.00} from XXXX XXXX. The terms were that if the flights were canceled within XXXX hours they were fully refundable. Our plans changed, so I canceled the flights within the XXXX hour time period and received an email from XXXX ( attached ) on XX/XX/XXXX stating that the full amount of {$1900.00} would be refunded to my credit card. 

Over XXXX weeks passed and only {$320.00} had been credited to my account. First, I called XXXX XXXX, but they said XXXX had to tell them the amount that needed to be refunded, as I did not book the flights with XXXX directly but through XXXX, so there was nothing they could do unless they hard from XXXX. I called XXXX and they acknowledged that I canceled the flights within the XXXX hour time period and was entitled to the full refund of {$1900.00}. They said it could take up to XXXX months for the full amount to be refunded. They also said that it was possible the credit card company already had the funds but were withholding them. 

I called the credit card company, FNBO ( an XXXX credit card ) and they said XXXX had only sent the {$320.00}, so on XX/XX/XXXX I filed a dispute. There was some confusion, as the charges were listed on my credit card as XXXX separate charges of {$650.00} ( as opposed to the total amount paid of {$1900.00} stated in the XXXX email as the refund amount ). I was told I needed to file three separate disputes for each charge separately -- that is, three different disputes in the amount of {$650.00} each, but one of those had to take into account the difference between the amount already refunded ( {$320.00} ) and the remainder owed, which was {$330.00}. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, the first {$650.00} was credited to my account. On XXXX XXXX, the remaining {$330.00} was credited to my account for the second charge. However, on XXXX XXXX the final refund amount of {$650.00} was credited on to my account, but then reversed by FNBO and recharged to my account again for the final {$650.00}. 

I called the FNBO dispute department and they said XXXX 's policy was that flights were non-refundable. I explained that all three flights were booked at the same time and canceled at the same time ( within the XXXX hour time frame ), so why would XXXX flights be refundable and not the third? I sent FNBO disputes the email from XXXX that stated the full amount should be refunded ( {$1900.00} ) and explained the situation again as a new dispute, but FNBO said my cases were closed and there was nothing more they could do for me. 

So, they insisted I would NOT receive a refund for the final {$650.00}, and this amount remained on my card. I paid it off because I didn't want to pay interest on money I didn't actually owe and I waited, hoping XXXX would send the full refund to FNBO, they would see their mistake, and finally refund the full amount. However, by XX/XX/year> the money was still not refunded. Hence my complaint here, to the CFPB.

THE TRANSACTION In a credit card securitization transaction only the receivables are sold, not the accounts that generate the receivables. The financial institution retains legal ownership of the credit card accounts and can continue to change the terms on the accounts. Accounts corresponding to securitized loans are typically referred to as the designated accounts ( or sometimes trust accounts ). The initial outstanding balances on the designated accounts are sold to the trust as are the rights to any new charges on the designated accounts. Subsequently, as cardholder purchase activity generates more receivables on the designated accounts, these new receivables are purchased by the trust from the originating institution/seller/transferor. The trust uses the monthly principal payments received from the cardholders to acquire these new charges or receivables. When the securitization is initially set up, the originating institution/seller adds sufficient receivables to support the principal balance of the certificates plus an additional amount ( seller 's interest ) that serves to absorb fluctuations in the outstanding balance of the receivables. The originating institution/seller will make subsequent additions to the trust in order to keep the seller 's interest at the required level. On XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX, a {$2800.00} charge posted to my Citi XXXX XXXX credit card. 2 days later, I disputed this transaction. The merchant name in question is presented as " XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX '' and the transaction was a Card Not Present - Keyed In transaction that took place in Florida.

Furthermore, I see that they withdrew that FULL amount from my checking account, which was set up for XXXX.

For one, no one reached out to me after the dispute, I was always calling ahead and making sure everything was fine. At every step, they assured me that everything was fine, when in reality, it ultimately resulted in a negative outcome. Secondly, I am under the impression that Citi is deliberately skirting Regulation E by marking the investigation as closed so that the dispute count-down will reset. In any case, I do not think Citi 's internal human + technological systems are adequate for this day and age. Their systems are adversarial to the consumer, and I recommend the CFPB investigating Citi 's adherence to regulations, especially Regulation E, as well as adherence to basic technological standards that protects consumers from Fraud investigations.

THE TRANSACTION In a credit card securitization transaction only the receivables are sold, not the accounts that generate the receivables. The financial institution retains legal ownership of the credit card accounts and can continue to change the terms on the accounts. Accounts corresponding to securitized loans are typically referred to as the designated accounts ( or sometimes trust accounts ). The initial outstanding balances on the designated accounts are sold to the trust as are the rights to any new charges on the designated accounts. Subsequently, as cardholder purchase activity generates more receivables on the designated accounts, these new receivables are purchased by the trust from the originating institution/seller/transferor. The trust uses the monthly principal payments received from the cardholders to acquire these new charges or receivables. When the securitization is initially set up, the originating institution/seller adds sufficient receivables to support the principal balance of the certificates plus an additional amount ( seller 's interest ) that serves to absorb fluctuations in the outstanding balance of the receivables. The originating institution/seller will make subsequent additions to the trust in order to keep the seller 's interest at the required level. Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank regarding its handling of a credit card dispute involving a charge of {$1200.00}. I believe Chases actions have failed to uphold my rights under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( XXXX ), as it has unreasonably refused to accept sufficient evidence substantiating my claim and has shown bias toward the merchant, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( the Merchant ). 
On XX/XX/year>, I made a payment of {$2500.00} to XXXX XXXX XXXX for a service. The payment was made using XXXX different cards. {$1300.00} was charged on my debit card and {$1200.00} to my chase credit card. When I picked up the car and drove it home, It was clear that not all the service requested and paid for was completed. The most critical issue which was the car vibrating with a loud noise when stationary and XXXX XXXX mode was unresolved. I reported the issue to the merchant abut they told me they can not fix the issue and recommended I go to the car dealer. At this point, I requested a refund, but the merchant refused. The XXXX failed to deliver the services as agreed. I initiated a dispute with Chase for {$1200.00} which was the cost for the unresolved issue. I believe that the charge was unauthorized due to non-performance by the XXXX. Chase required me to submit supporting evidence, which I did. 

I provided XXXX key documents to substantiate my claim : A Technical Service Bulletin issued by XXXX XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/year>, which clearly indicated that I was at their location for an unresolved service issue beyond the date the initial service should have been completed. The XXXX acknowledgment on this document confirms that the service was not successfully rendered. 

An invoice from a second mechanic who inspected my vehicle after the unresolved service. This invoice documents the issues and estimates the repair cost, thereby supporting my claim that XXXX did not complete the service I paid for. The second mechanic, however, declined to issue a letter, as they believed the invoice provided was sufficient, accurate, and professional documentation. 
Despite submitting this evidence, Chase closed the dispute and sided with the XXXX, requesting that I provide an additional letter from the second mechanic. Chases refusal to accept the invoice constitutes unfair treatment, violates my rights under the XXXX, and undermines my ability to recover my disputed funds. 
Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, consumers are entitled to dispute billing errors on credit card statements, including charges for goods and services not delivered as agreed. The law requires that the creditor conduct a reasonable investigation and provide a fair and impartial review of the evidence presented by the consumer. This conduct not only hinders my ability to resolve this dispute but also violates my consumer rights.

( a ) With respect to extensions of credit made on credit card accounts, a bank may charge and collect interest at an annual rate not exceeding thirty percent ( 30 % ) per year or at an equivalent daily, weekly, monthly, or quarterly rate.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Thank you in advance for taking the time to read my letter and process my dispute case. 

I am writing to re-open a dispute that I filed in XX/XX/year> for a purchase made at XXXX XXXX. The previous dispute, which has been closed by Chase, was filed under an incorrect reason chargeback code 13.7 ( Canceled merchandise / services ). This was likely an error from the Chase representative I had spoken to when opening the dispute. I would like to re-open the dispute under the correct reason code, 13.3 ( Not as described or Defective Merchandise/Services ). 

I have attached two documents. One is the letter I sent to Chase in the initial dispute. The second is the letter I sent to Chase after they closed my initial dispute, having misunderstood the chargeback code that should have applied to my dispute. 

***Merchandise or services are not the same as your verbal description*** We were measured for 2 suits, 2 dress shirts, a winter coat, and a dress at XXXX XXXX physical store location. XXXX XXXX employees repeatedly assured us that they were certified clothing producers for XXXX and that the clothing we received would be XXXX brand and quality. They also made claims to the fabric quality, saying that the suits and coat would be 100 % cashmere wool, and the would be silk. 
When we received the merchandise a few days later, the clothing did not match the description. The clothing was cheaply made, using synthetic materials like polyester. The clothing was not XXXX brand like they claimed it would be. Additionally, the clothing fit very poorly, despite the measurements taken of us while we were in the store. 

XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX made us sign waivers after we had paid for the merchandise in order to protect themselves from chargeback disputes. However, note that we had not received any merchandise upon signing these waivers. Please be advised that all of the photographic waiver evidence XXXX XXXX provides to Chase were waivers I had signed AFTER we paid for the product but BEFORE it was received. 

The waivers state : - I hereby acknowledge that I have chosen the styles, colors, and the quality of the fabrics myself and the products will be produced according to my size, measurements and specifications. 
- As I have made all the decisions myself, I also understand that XXXX XXXX is an independent private tailoring company and not affiliated or under influence of any brand names. 
- As all above mentioned clothes are custom made for my size, I acknowledge that XXXX XXXX maintains No Refund Policy, under any circumstances. I am happy and satisfied with my payment and merchandise Effective immediately. I also agree not to make any disputes through my bank or otherwise after this transaction - I acknowledge satisfactory receipt of relative goods and services Again, this waiver was signed immediately after I had paid for the clothing, but the merchandise had not been received since it was going to be custom made days later. This is misleading in many ways : - First, the quality of fabrics that we were shown during the sale was not the same fabric used to create the clothing. We could not possibly say we are satisfied with the purchase before we even received the products- Second, the entire time we were in the store, XXXX XXXX employees were showing us XXXX catalogs from which we could choose which style and color of clothing we wanted. I asked them multiple times, and they assured us they were a certified producer for XXXX, and that they would be making us the same clothes they produced for XXXX XXXX. Therefore everything they were saying about the brand and the quality of the clothing was a lie and used as a tactic to make us agree to a purchase. This was also the only reason I agreed to pay {$1500.00} for this clothing. A non-branded custom suit from a Thai tailor costs less than {$100.00}. And since the waiver was given to me after I had made the payment, I essentially had no choice but to sign at that point. 
- XXXX, XXXX XXXX states a No Refund Policy and a No dispute policy. Consumer protection laws classify this type of policy as illegal, and not enforceable, especially in cases where the merchandise has been gravely misrepresented. 

- Lastly, I could not have possibly acknowledged satisfactory receipt of relative goods and services- I signed this waiver when I paid for the clothing, which was a few days before XXXX XXXX made the clothes. 

***Attempts to resolve with merchant*** After I had made the payment and left the store, I became suspicious of what had just happened. I looked up their store online and I saw many reviews online saying they were a scam operation, and that other customers received clothing completely different than what they were promised. I went back into the store minutes later to tell them I no longer wanted the clothes but they were firm in asserting their no return policy. At this point, the merchant seemed intent on keeping our money no matter what. It is hard to prove I went back to the store to cancel the purchase, but I did make a good faith attempt to cancel the purchase before they started making the clothing. 
Thank you for taking the time to consider my dispute case. I hope, with this additional information, we can come to a fair conclusion.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint against Citibank regarding the improper closure of my account, discriminatory practices, and failure to validate an alleged debt. I believe Citibanks actions violate several federal and state consumer protection laws, including : Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ) New York General Business Law ( GBL ) section 349 Details of the Issue : 1. I opened my account with Citibank on XX/XX/2023, and it was abruptly closed in XX/XX/2023 without sufficient explanation or notice. 
2. Citibank representatives claim the account was closed because I refused to pay, which is untrue. I was exercising my right to dispute a payment under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), not refusing to pay. Disputing a payment is a protected right and does not constitute grounds for account closure. 
3. Citibank representatives stated that my account is in collections, even though the account was not in default at the time of closure. This is a misrepresentation of the accounts status and may constitute a violation of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) if such information was reported to credit bureaus. 
4. The closure of my account while I was disputing a charge appears retaliatory and discriminatory, violating the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), which prohibits creditors from taking adverse action against consumers for exercising their rights. 
Relevant Legal Violations : 1. Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ) : Citibanks closure of my account while I was disputing a payment constitutes discrimination and retaliation for exercising my consumer rights under federal law. 
2. Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) : The FCBA protects consumers who dispute billing errors. Citibank failed to properly address my dispute before closing the account, which violates my rights under this law. 
3. Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) : Citibanks claim that my account is in collections, despite it not being in default, constitutes a violation of the FDCPA, as it is a misrepresentation of the debts status. 
Additionally, I have requested validation of the alleged debt. If Citibank can not validate the debt, they must cease all collection efforts immediately. 
4. Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) : The TILA requires lenders to provide clear and transparent information about credit accounts. Citibank failed to provide adequate notice or explanation for the account closure, potentially violating this law. 
5. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) : If Citibank has reported my account as delinquent or in collections to credit bureaus, this constitutes a violation of the FCRA because the account was not in default. 
6. Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ) : Citibanks actionsclosing my account without justification, misrepresenting the accounts status, and failing to address my disputeconstitute unfair, deceptive, or abusive practices ( UDAAPs ), which are prohibited under the CFPA. 
7. New York General Business Law ( GBL ) section 349 : As a resident of New York, I am also protected under GBL section 349, which prohibits deceptive business practices. Citibanks misrepresentation of my accounts status and unjustified closure may violate this state law. 

My Requests : I request that Citibank : 1. Provide a legitimate explanation for the closure of my account. 
2. Produce the original signed contract for my account. 
3. Provide the chain of titles or ownership records for my account to verify its status. 
4. Validate any alleged debt associated with the account. If they can not validate the debt, they must cease and desist all collection activity and remove any inaccurate reporting from my credit file.

When my Dad wrote to Citi to ask how they could justify closing his accounts when he acted based on Citi employee 's advice, their response was to say that they had an absolute right to close credit card accounts. 
The Government has no legal responsibility to regulate in any given area.

In the absence of them lying to customers or taking other improper actions, Citi is free to close a credit card for " any reason or no reason '', The issue is not whether Citi can close a credit card or whether they can close bank accounts that they are worried are money laundering.

Beyond the specifics of customers being harmed by this practice there is a broader issue : permitting Cit to continue their mistraining sends Citi the message that they can mistrain employees, cause eserious harm to customers in othe rareras and get away with it.

Sending that message is not my idea of why we have the CFPB, hopefully it isi not yours either.

Issue: Advertising and marketing, including promotional offers
Sub-issue: Didn't receive advertised or promotional terms
Consumer complaint narrative:
Hi there, This complaint involves XXXX parties that are both refusing accountability and directing me to the opposite party for resolution. 

This complaint will be copied and resubmitted - one for Credit Karma, XXXX for XXXX. This complaint will be submitted against Credit Karma. 

I logged into creditkarma.com and received a promotional offer to transfer the balance of my high-interest XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 29.9 % interest ) to a lower interest card ( see screenshot ). 

The card recommended by Credit Karma was another XXXX card. I clicked the referral link Credit Karma provided and went through the application process at chase.com. 

During the application process at chase.com, XXXX requested the account number of the card I intended to to transfer the balance from, as well as the amount I wanted to transfer. 

I entered the account number of the XXXX XXXX XXXX card, as well as the amount ( {$5000.00} ). 

I entered that information, clicked " continue '' and was then notified that my application was accepted and I was enrolled in a new card with a credit limit of {$1500.00} ( I was expecting {$5000.00} and there was no " confirm '' button to accept enrollment with this credit limit - it simply enrolled me immediately ). 

After I was enrolled in the card, I reached out to XXXX about this, and they informed me that my balance transfer was ineligible, as XXXX does not allow the transfer of balances between cards that they administer. As the original card was a XXXX XXXX XXXX card, and my new card was a XXXX card, the new card was essentially useless to me. Furthermore, there would be hard-pulls on my credit profiles that would not be rescinded. Neither XXXX nor Credit Karma agreed to provided supplemental documentation for my appeal to the credit bureaus. 

I asked for more information, and XXXX indicated that this policy is quite common across lending institution- to prohibit customers from openeing new cards at the same bank and transferring balances between them. 

When I mentioned that the application process included inputting the original high-interest card account number ( XXXX XXXX XXXX card ) and a balance transfer amount, and the application under the auspices of a balance transfer was accepted, despite XXXX explicitly requesting the information that it should have used to inform the consumer of balance transfer ineligibility, XXXX indicated that the policy regarding balance transfers is in their terms and conditions. XXXX told me to take it up with Credit Karma, as the promotional offer should never have been suggested. 

I reached out to credit karma over email, instant messaging, and phone, carefully detailing the situation as a means to prevent this from happening to other customers, and to request supporting documentation for when I submit an appeal to the credit bureaus have the hard pull removed from my profiles. Their reply to all these requests has been unchanging : " XXXX XXXX, I understand you do not feel that the offer was represented properly on our site. 

The offers you see are provided and vetted by the lender / credit card company. The terms and conditions of those cards are managed by the credit card companies and not by Credit Karma. 

Unfortunately, the terms and conditions set forth by the lender and are subject to change at the lenders discretion. 

Regards, Credit Karma Member Support '' So here we are - XXXX is blaming Credit Karma, Credit Karma is blaming chase, and they are both making money off this abusive process that results in material harm to the consumer ( negative marks on the credit profile ). 

In closing Credit Karma should not be promoting offers for balance transfers that are ineligible - whether it is simple negligence or bad-faith, they have a responsibility to adhere to industry-wide standards. 

XXXX should not be allowing a consumer to complete a new card XXXX  balance transfer bundled application ( in this case presented to the consumer as a singular product ), especially after requesting the account number of the source high-interest card, and then NOT using that to inform the consumer of ineligibility before enrolling the consumer in the card. 

This submission will be used for Credit Karma, I will submit another one against XXXX after completeing this one.

Issue: Advertising and marketing, including promotional offers
Sub-issue: Didn't receive advertised or promotional terms
Consumer complaint narrative:
I called Chase to inquire about their " Pay Over Time '' plan which, from time to time, has promotional offers tied to its use. In specific, I was interested in using the plan to pay for my daughters ' tuition, {$26000.00}, but pay off the charge over time ( in this case, 24 months, as was offered ). 

I have two cards with Chase, a Southwest card and a XXXX XXXX, and have used this program once already on my Southwest card. Thus, I am very familiar with how the program works. 

Prior to making this payment to the school, I called to confirm that this promotion was still active, and, crucially, that I was still eligible given that I had already used the promotion on one of my two cards. I was assured that since I have not used the promotion on my second card, that I would be eligible for the same program - no interest, no fees for 24 months so long as I make the monthly installment ( i.e., 1/24th of that charge every month ). I asked the Chase representative to repeat herself and confirmed it twice over. There was no misunderstanding about what I was told. 

Subsequent to that conversation I went to the schools website and made my payment. All of this took place on or about XX/XX/year>. 

When I logged into my account on Monday, XX/XX/XXXX so I could opt into the Pay Over Time plan, sure enough that feature was there, but the payment plan now included {$300.00} in monthly fees. This amounts to {$7300.00} over the life of the loan, or an effective interest rate of 24.41 %. 

I immediately called the bank to resolve this issue. The agent heard my complaint, was apologetic, but said that he could not resolve my issue at the time. Instead, he would need to request that the recording of my XX/XX/XXXX conversation be pulled and open a formal investigation. This was great news, as I was 100 % certain that the tape would confirm my story. 

I did not receive a return call from Chase. 

I then called back on Friday, XX/XX/XXXX and spoke with a supervising agent named XXXX. He told me that, in fact, the previous agent did not request a recording of the initial call, and that an investigation had not been initiated. He, too, was apologetic, and committed to doing both of those things himself. He then committed to calling me back on Monday, XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX pm. I had plans to travel that day, but rescheduled my flight to ensure I could dedicate the necessary time to my conversation with XXXX. XXXX did not call me back as promised. 

At XXXX XXXX  of that day, after waiting in vain for XXXX call, I called and spoke with another agent. This time, the agent found a note that I had called on the previous Friday, but there was no mention of XXXX commitment to calling me back with the findings from his investigation. This new agent helped me file a new complaint related to my being dismissed and lied to by XXXX. She further confirmed that an investigation would commence. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I called back to inquire. This time, I again was told that no recording had been requested, and was further told that there were no notes about XXXX commitment to call me. I was then informed that all of this was entirely fruitless given that there was nothing the team could do to help, and that the only people who might be able to help me were located in Chase Banks Executive Office. 

I then called the Chase Executive Office and lodged a formal complaint ( Case # : XXXX ) which was assigned to a case manager, XXXX ( not sure on spelling ). I opened this case with XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. 

I called to speak with XXXX on Friday, XX/XX/XXXX, and was told by a receptionist that she would return my call that day. She did not. 

I called her multiple times over the subsequent days, until finally connecting with her on Tuesday, XX/XX/XXXX. In that conversation she committed to doing an investigation, and returning my call. 

Mercifully, XXXX did as she promised, and got back to a week later, XX/XX/XXXX, with the conclusion of her investigation. I was told a number of contradictory, misleading, and incorrect things during the course of that conversation ( I will note, that XXXX was incredibly professional, and I harbor no ill-will towards her whatsoever ). 

Among other things, XXXX said the following : 1. She could not find any recordings from my previous conversations. Very upsetting, and very convenient, I might add. Also, it seemed rather easy for her to pull these recordings in fact, we looked at other days when I called and on those too, she found no recordings. Odd, certainly, but especially odd given I had been told on XX/XX/XXXX, prior to reaching out to the Chase Executive office, that it takes 15 days for recordings to be pulled.

2. She told me that even if she could find the recordings, the only purpose those would serve would be in training Chases agents against providing similarly misleading advice in future conversations with other clients of the bank. This was incredibly odd because ( a ) I was offered this on XX/XX/XXXX for the express purpose of helping me resolve my issue, and ( b ) according to XXXX, it was irrelevant what the agent had told me because the bank was not willing to honor the advice I had been given under any circumstance. This begs the questions, why string me along and offer to investigate at all? And why bother training the agents if the advice they are giving is entirely irrelevant anyhow? 
3. I was encouraged by XXXX to go into a Chase bank to discuss the promotional plans next time prior to making a purchase to ensure there was no misunderstanding. But at the same time, she told me, even if the agents in the bank gave me bad advice, or otherwise misled me, I would be on the hook to pay off the charge in whatever way Chase deemed me responsible. Which begs the question of why would I ever go into the bank for support if that, too, could end up being part of the problem, and that the bank would not honor the assurances of its agents. 

I had been very clear that I wanted to pay my charge in accordance with the plan I was offered, and that I wanted to resolve the issue before the billing cycle closed on XX/XX/XXXX. Of course, due to all the back and forth notably, me following up numerous times, and being ignored by agents for a month by the time this investigation was concluded, the billing cycle had closed, and now I am being asked to either come up with $ XXXX or just commit to paying $ XXXX in fees over the course of the payment plan. Neither of these options are fair, reasonable or satisfactory. 

After doing a quick search online, I have found many other people who have had similar issues with Chase bank related to their Pay Over Time plan. Mine issue is unique in that I called in advance of using said plan, and only did so with their guidance and still, I am being abused. 

But, even when the plan works, it is itself misleading and predatory. The introductory offer is advertised as no interest or fees for 24 months. The subsequent charges are then advertised as having only a fixed monthly fee not interest, get it? - that amounts to nearly the same interest rate that the card offers to begin with ( in my case, 24 % vs. 28 % ). The intent of these promotions is to lure people into the plan, and then have them default on what seems like a very compelling idea upfront ; I dont mean to sound cynical, but Chase is certainly not offering people this plan out of the goodness of their heart. 

In my situation, its all the more frustrating because I communicated directly with the bank to ensure the plan would work as needed, and when it didnt, I was promised a resolution that required me to run around after their agents for a month, only to be told that the bank was unwilling to rectify this situation, despite the obvious errors ( and worse ) made on its part, and the serious impact it had on me personally. 

All I am seeking is the ability to pay off my charge as promised, using the payment plan that is currently active on other Chase credit cards, including my Southwest card.

These violations contradict House Joint Resolution 192 ( HJR 192 ), Public Law 73-10 ( Emergency Banking Act ), the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ), the U.S. Constitution, and various federal laws and regulations. 
Detailed Summary of Violations : Failure to Honor Securities and Lawful Payment Instruments : I tendered lawful payments using securities and negotiable instruments provided by BANK OF AMERICA, N.A., such as bills, statements, equity checks, bearer bonds, and coupons attached to the statements. According to UCC 3-104 ( a ) and UCC 3-302 ( a ) ( 2 ), these instruments are valid as negotiable instruments, and I accepted these securities " for value, '' issuing a restrictive endorsement as outlined in UCC 3-206. Additionally, I affixed postage stamps ( lawful money ) to these securities under HJR 192 and UCC 1-201 ( b ) ( 24 ), reinforcing my payments. 
Despite receiving these securities through registered and certified mail, BANK OF AMERICA , N.A . failed to discharge the debt, return the securities, or properly credit my account, in violation of UCC 3-603 ( b ). Florida Statute 559.72 ( 3 ) under the Consumer Collection Practices Act ( CCPA ) expressly prohibits the use of deceptive or unfair trade practices in the denial of financial services. XXXX. XXXX. Failure to Recognize My Capacity to Contract My capacity to contract is a key element in this matter, as American Express has disregarded my lawful standing to enter into a valid credit agreement. I have demonstrated my ability and willingness to engage in such agreements by fully complying with the legal standards governing credit applications, including the submission of lawful tender under the Federal Reserve Act. Therefore, the denial of my application, despite my clear ability to contract, constitutes an unlawful obstruction and discriminatory practice.

( 5 ) A reflection on a periodic statement of a computational or similar error of an accounting nature that is made by the creditor.

( 6 ) A reflection on a periodic statement of an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence.

I am filing a complaint regarding misleading and deceptive financing terms for a furniture purchase I made. Note that I have requested the original purchase agreement, but I can't even see my old statements to know the total amount I paid, so I will have some generalizations on prices in this complaint. The company will have the exact details on record. 

In 2021, I purchased furniture from Ashley Furniture under what I was told was a 60-month 0 % interest financing plan, which is common for Ashley. Both my wife and I were clearly informed by the salesperson that the entire purchase would be interest-free for 60 months. Based on this representation, we proceeded with the purchase, setting up the autopay for the minimum payments we were told were needed to complete the purchase with zero interest. I have been paying via autopay ever since. 

Only recently, I reviewed my financing statement more closely and discovered that the financing was split into two parts : one portion of the balance was subject to the 60-month 0 % interest plan as stated, but another portion of approximately {$4000.00} was only interest-free for 12 months. After those 12 months expired, I began incurring interest at an exorbitant rate of 30 %, resulting in thousands of dollars of additional interest charges, which I was unaware of at the time of purchase. 

The contract does mention the 12-month interest-free portion, but this critical detail was never explained to me by the salesperson. Both my wife and I relied on the salespersons clear verbal assurances that the financing would be 0 % interest for 60 months on the entire purchase. At no point were we told that a portion of the sale would only be interest-free for 12 months, nor were we provided with specific information about how much needed to be paid during those 12 months to avoid high interest charges. Had we been told this, we would have made adjustments to how much we paid to ensure we didn't pay interest, or walked away from the purchase altogether. 

As mentioned, based on the salespersons representations, I made minimum payments, believing that doing so would cover the balance and complete the purchase within the 60-month 0 % interest period. I was never informed that the 12-month portion would need to be paid off in full within that period to avoid high interest charges. This lack of disclosure significantly misled me, as I had no reason to believe there was any urgency in paying off a portion of the balance sooner. 

The salesperson who assisted us is no longer employed by the company, but this misrepresentation has caused significant financial harm. I believe this constitutes misleading and deceptive business practices. The purposeful failure to disclose the full terms of the financing arrangement is unfair and has resulted in substantial, unexpected costs for my family. 

I request that this issue be investigated and that the excessive interest charges be refunded or credited to my balance, and that the remaining balance be set to zero interest on the initial promise of 60 month payoff.

XXXX XXXX XXXX Last 4 of account XXXX XXXX XXXX Comenity Capital Bank I am writing to formally file a complaint against XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX credit card for what I believe to be unfair and deceptive practices related to their payment processing system and the imposition of late fees.

However, I was forced to schedule the payment for the following day due to a cutoff time imposed by the bank based on their time zone, which was not aligned with my local time. 3. Deceptive Practice of Waiving Fees Only After Account Closure Request : When I called the customer service department to dispute the late fees, I was initially denied any relief. It was only after I requested to close my account that the representative agreed to waive the fees. This tactic feels like a coercive and deceptive practice designed to retain customers by offering fee waivers only when the threat of account closure is imminent. Such behavior not only undermines trust but also puts consumers in a situation where they are forced to endure unfair treatment unless they take drastic measures like closing their accounts. 

Conclusion : I believe the actions taken by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX credit card, including the limitations of their payment processing system, the charging of late fees on top of other late fees, and the manipulative practice of waiving fees only upon account closure requests, constitute unfair and deceptive practices that violate consumer protection laws.

According to 15 U.S.C. 1691 ( d ), creditors are required to provide specific reasons for denying a credit application. Additionally, under 12 C.F.R. 1002.9 ( a ) ( 2 ), this explanation must clearly outline the factors that adversely affected my application. Furthermore, it is important to note that under the ECOA and Regulation B, credit decisions can not be based solely on credit scores. In your denial notice, it was suggested that my credit score played a significant role in your decision. As such, I would like to emphasize that the use of a credit score, while a factor in the evaluation process, should not be the sole determining factor in the denial of credit, as per the regulations mentioned.

Consumer complaint narrative:
After a large-scale data breach, we had set up security alerts on our credit. On XX/XX/year>, I was alerted through this process that a JetBlue Credit Card had been taken out in my name through Barclay 's US of Delaware. We immediately called, confirmed and cancelled this card. We were told there were several travel charges, which I assumed would be therefore be cancelled. 

A few days later, we received a physical letter confirming the account was suspended along with information that my email could not be confirmed. A day or XXXX later, a physical copy of the Barclay 's JetBlue Card arrived, which I again confirmed was closed and pending investigation. I destroyed the card but retained its number for my records. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, however, I received a text message about a delay and Gate Change on an international flight out of XXXX. I was in at home thousands of miles away. I contacted JetBlue, and they were unable to provide a traveler who had been paid for under my name without a reservation number. I contacted Detectives with XXXX XXXX Police who confirmed no one was using flying under my name, they recommended contacting Jet Blue. This was XXXX weeks after the account was suspended. 

Then, on XX/XX/XXXX, another text arrived about a Gate Change on the return flight. I again attempted to contact Jet Blue, but again without an itinerary or ticket number, they could not provide a name. Nor would they connect me directly to their security office or cc me on an email to their security office.

An hour and a half after calling Jet Blue, with the Flight en route, they have not contacted me. I could provide them with outgoing and incoming Flight numbers, my number, and the card number on file, so they can check manifests and investigate, but they have not taken action. The Representative did suggest I contact Barclay 's. I did so, but they can not provide any names on the XXXX (! ) tickets purchased on the fraudulent account the day it opened, nor the itineraries. They could also not provide the email account associated with the application -- because there wasn't one! 

The XXXX XXXX XXXX had already explained that the traveler may also be a victim who had booked through a fraudulent travel agency, but it is ridiculous that neither JetBlue nor Barclay 's retains records of names paid for by third parties, that Barclay 's allows same-day charges on just-opened accounts without a card arriving or an email account, and that all charges ( and their flights ) were not immediately canceled While Barclay 's assures me that I am not liable " pending investigation '', consumers as a whole are impacted by allowing thousands of charges to go unreversed, and by not retaining records sufficient for law enforcement to investigate.

Given that literally billions of people are now compromised, the following immediate steps should be taken : 1 ) Jet Blue airlines should make available the names traveling under any other name 's account in cases such as this. 
2 ) Barclay 's US should not allow thousands in credit and XXXX separate transactions on the day a card is applied for with confirming via US mail that this credit was sought.

3 ) Barclay 's and/or JetBlue should retain records of all transactions under a specific card number. 

Again, I assume my diligence will result in me not being liable, but their shoddiness has in fact enabled the perpetrators of fraud, and cost me hours of my time while increasing costs to consumers through the inevitable write-offs and investigations their negligence has caused.

Sub-issue: Charged too much interest
Consumer complaint narrative:
I've had a credit card with what is now known as Citi for more than 40 years. It's the first card I ever had. I have never missed a payment. In its current form, its an XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. In XX/XX/year>, I took a {$20000.00} loan on the card at 9.99 %. It's called a XXXX  XXXX Citi XXXX XXXX. The minimum monthly payment is just under {$430.00}. I set up an autopay from a XXXX XXXX checking account to take care of that portion of my monthly statement. I continued to use the card for standard purchases ( currently at 28.24 % ), and I paid off those purchases in full every month from a XXXX XXXX checking account. So, the only interest I should be paying is the interest on the XXXX XXXX. 

A number of months went by and suddenly they started charging interest on purchases, even though I had paid the previous month 's purchase charges in full. Numerous people in " customer service '' told me that as long as I am carrying another balance on the account, I will always be charged interest on purchases. Even when I quoted the following to them ( this appears on every monthly statement ), they were adamant : " We will not charge you interest on purchases if you pay your monthly Citi XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX plus your entire balance, excluding any Citi Flex Plan balances, by the due date each month. '' It's obvious that the people I dealt with were confusing the rules around balance transfer balances with those that apply to the Citi XXXX XXXX. 

In XXXX of this year, following the death of my mother-in-law, my wife used the card to pay a total of {$10000.00} in funeral home expenses. Those charges were posted to the purchases portion of the account, as they should have been. As soon as we received proceeds from a life insurance policy, and feeling quite uncomfortable with a {$10000.00} charge sitting on my account, I made an online payment to Citi for {$10000.00} on XX/XX/XXXX. My mistake, apparently, was that I didn't wait until I had received the next month 's statement with the {$10000.00} in charges on it. So they applied the {$10000.00} payment not to the Purchases balance ( 28.24 % ) but to the Flex Plan balance ( 9.99 % ). As a result, even though I continued to pay in full for all of the purchases I made on the card, I have been charged hundreds of dollars in " standard purchase '' interest charges every month. ( I have stopped using the card until this is resolved. ) I have explained on the phone numerous times that my intention was that the {$10000.00} payment be applied to the standard purchase balance, which included the {$10000.00} funeral charges. XXXX person ( a supervisor ) told me on XXXX XXXX she would request that the {$10000.00} be applied to the purchase balance instead of to the XXXX XXXX balance, but she wasn't making any promises. 

Having heard nothing from Citi, I called again on XXXX XXXX, and a person who said her name was XXXX noted the call I had made on XXXX XXXX. She couldn't explain why there had been no follow-up. She agreed that the {$10000.00} payment should have gone to my Purchase balance, not to the Flex Plan balance. And she said the higher interest charged on the Purchase balance should be refunded. This was the first bit of encouraging news I have received since this saga began. 

On Tuesday, XXXX XXXX, I received a form letter stating that " payment amounts greater than the minimum due are applied to balances with higher APRs before balances with lower rates. Billed segments will be paid before unbilled segments. '' In other words, if you are late with your payment, it will cost you ( which I totally understand ) AND if you are early with your payment, it will cost you. The distinction here is that the {$10000.00} charge had been placed on my account, but it hadn't been billed to me yet in a statement. 

I think they are so far behind that the letter I received on XXXX XXXX was not addressing the conversation I had on XXXX XXXX but the previous one. So, there's hope that XXXX is still trying to do something. But I am not counting on it. 

All I want from Citi is for them to move that {$10000.00} payment from the Flex Plan side of the ledger to the Standard Purchases side, which was my intention to begin with. I will happily continue paying on the Flex Plan loan every month until it is paid off.

Consumer complaint narrative:
On XX/XX/year> I sent over a payment to Chase, they refused to accept my form of payment, I have no received any written response nor a form of resolution, below are laws that they are violating. 

Under 15 U.S.C. 1666 ( b ), part of the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), consumers are provided with the right to dispute billing errors, including unauthorized charges, errors in the amount charged, or charges for goods or services that were not received. This statute lays out the procedures for disputing a billing error and the obligations of the creditor when handling such disputes. 

A creditor shall not, prior to the end of the time period allowed for payment of undisputed amounts, report that an amount or amounts in dispute under this section are delinquent because the amount or amounts remain unpaid. ( 12 CFR 226.13 ( e ) ) Regulation Z, part of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), governs the time of payment and ensures transparency in credit and billing practices. It includes rules on dispute resolution, billing error correction, and the time limits for creditors to respond. 

The payment due date must be clearly disclosed, and any penalties for late payments must be specified. 

Disputes over the timing or application of payments are covered under the dispute resolution procedures mentioned in 15 U.S.C. 1666 ( b ).

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am reporting Alphaeon Credit for predatory business practices and for failing to disclose clear information about their promotional plans. 

In XXXX, I saw a dentist to help treat my XXXX  XXXX who recommended XXXX. My insurance covered only a portion of it, so {$4500.00} was left for me to pay. The dentist opened a line of credit through Alphaeon to finance the procedure. For over 2 years, I have diligently made payments to Alphaeon, reducing my payment down from {$4500.00} with interest to a little over {$1800.00}. 

However, in XX/XX/XXXX, my balance had skyrocketed to over {$4000.00} again! Confused, I contacted Alphaeon to find out if this was a mistake. But it wasn't. Apparently, the " promotional plan '' I had unknowingly been under had ended, and I hadn't paid off the balance in full. Granted, I'd had no idea about this plan. I told the representative such, but all he said was it was in my monthly statements. 

The problem is, I barely read my paper statements! I just pay online, for the most part, and whenever I did open them, it was only to glance at the first page with the amount due and remaining balance, every so often. 

I explained to the representative that they have access to my phone and email, and that they have sent me emails and text messages in the past to inquire about any late payments. Why hadn't they notified me of this promotional plan through text or email, warning that the end of the plan was near and what the consequences are if I don't pay the amount in full by the due date. 

The only answer I received was that I should've read my statements, and that it can't be reversed. 

This is absolutely outrageous and extremely predatory. I worked hard to get that bill down and to think I have to start all over again over something I had no prior knowledge of? Something I wouldn't have even chosen had I known about it? Alphaeon Credit should not be allowed to take advantage of its customers this way, and they should not be allowed to operate with so little transparency.

I had to call and speak to XXXX different representatives, to get the issue cleared. This was the first time. 
The second time happened the exact same way. And with the exact same scenario. 
Interest fees on a closed unused credit card with a zeroed out balance. Four-five agents later, I have gotten a solution and the fees waived. Because it was not my burden. 
The THIRD, yes THIRD time I have attempted closing a credit card with Comenity, has proven to be the most frustrating and demeaning experience Ive ever dealt with. I called to close my comenity backed bank card with a very low line of credit on XX/XX/XXXX, and paid the total remaining amount of XXXX $ and change, when I called and paid the remaining balance that I was told by the representative, there was absolutely no mention of any fees being incurred, either late fees or interest fees. I was told the amount I paid was the proper amount to close the credit card. I was not told this when I paid the amount down to close it, otherwise I would have paid it as well. Who pays a credit card to close it and does not pay the late fee? One would think that the individual attempting to close the account would pay the ENTIRE amount including all fees at the point of payment and closing down the credit card. That was my intention when I called to make a final payment and close the account.

Better yet, the late fee has now gone to collections and is DOUBLE what the late fee was, and Im just now receiving word the account is even in collections. A month and a half later.

Upon receiving word the account was now in default because of the unknown late fee charge, I call the second time and speak to two representatives, one transferred me to a XXXX who was my supervising case manager he was absolutely condescending and interrupted everything I had to say, wouldnt let me speak and was hostile. I asked for his department manager, and was told he was the manager. I asked for a last name and was told that information couldnt be released. I asked to speak to another representative and he refused to transfer me, only to be hung up on.

I called back immediately and was addressed politely and handled respectfully. By two COMPLETELY different agents.

Again, to be told there was nothing they could do about the non discussed late fee, but I pushed it harder because I want to see a resolution to this, after more persistence and expression over my unhappiness over having to pay for someone elses mistake, I was told they are going to pull the first initial call, review it, and essentially see if I am telling the truth. This request is in accordance with the following laws and regulations : 1. The Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), 15 U.S.C. 1666 : This law stipulates that creditors must promptly credit or refund overpayments and correct billing errors, including unauthorized charges. The FCBA limits a cardholder 's liability for unauthorized use of their credit card to {$50.00}. 
2. The Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ), 15 U.S.C. 1693 : While primarily applicable to debit cards, this act also provides protections against fraudulent transactions and limits consumer liability for unauthorized electronic fund transfers.

3. The Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. : This act requires creditors to provide clear and accurate disclosures about the terms and costs of consumer credit, including how interest is calculated and when it is applied.

4. Regulation Z, 12 C.F.R. 226 : This regulation implements TILA and provides specific rules for credit card issuers, including how to handle billing errors and unauthorized use claims.

5. The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. : This act requires that credit reporting agencies and furnishers of information ( such as credit card companies ) ensure the accuracy of information in consumer credit reports.

Furthermore, I remind you of your obligations under the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, which prohibits unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ) in consumer financial products and services.

I request that you conduct a thorough investigation of this matter and provide a written explanation of your findings within 30 days, as required by the FCBA. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), consumers are entitled to fair and accurate reporting of their credit information. Additionally, the XXXX provisions protect consumers from unfair, deceptive, or abusive practices by financial institutions. The Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( XXXX ) ensures that all creditworthy applicants are treated fairly and prohibits discrimination in any aspect of a credit transaction. As a XXXX XXXX, I am concerned that Wells Fargos actions may also reflect discriminatory practices, which have historically affected minority communities. 

To resolve this issue, I propose that Wells Fargo restore my credit limit to its original amount and freeze my account without accruing interest for XXXX year, allowing me to pay off the balance. In exchange, I will agree to never knowingly request credit from Wells Fargo again. 

I request that the CFPB investigate this matter and take appropriate action to ensure that Wells Fargos practices comply with consumer protection laws. Additionally, I seek relief from the excessive interest charges and a review of the credit limit reduction process to prevent similar issues from affecting other consumers. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt response and resolution.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I have a Citibank card. It admittedly has a high balance. I got a cash advance well over a year ago, maybe longer.

I always pay more than the minimum payment, and I make the payment before the due date because I read that doing so avoids assessment of additional fees. Nonetheless, after I make the payment before the deadline, I'm immediately charged additional interest and fees for the card and for cash advances. For example, I made the early payment last week before the due date, which reduced my available balance to about {$290.00} However, my available balance today is {$180.00}. Here is the recent activity, to give you context : Payment on XX/XX/XXXX ( before due date ) : {$220.00} This was above the minimum due of {$150.00} Payment due date : XX/XX/XXXX Last statement balance : {$4500.00} Purchases : XXXX ( I have not made purchases in several months, if you need that info ) Cash advances : XXXX Fees : XXXX Interest charged to purchases : {$84.00} Interest charged to XXXX XXXX XX/XX/XXXX : {$27.00} ( I don't know what this is ) Total interest charged in XXXX is {$1000.00} The interest rate is 26.24 % on XXXX XXXX The interest rate on standard purchases and advances is 29.99 % I have not made any purchases since XX/XX/XXXX. 

I

chatted with a customer rep. I was told to avoid the additional interest charges and fees I have to make two consecutive payments to pay the balance in full. I'm not able to do that. The high rate of the interest and fees which are always added IMMEDIATELY after I make the early payment make it impossible to pay down the principal. I chatted with customer support " XXXX '' and the rep told me this : " This interest charge was billed as a remaining interest charge. This was billed as previous statement balances were not paid in full on or before the due date.

When the statement balance is not paid in full or a payment is late interest bills that month based on the average daily balance for that billing cycle. Then the following billing cycle the remaining interest charge is billed ; which is interest accrued from the time period the last statement cycled until we received complete payment in full again. To avoid future interest charges, we need to receive two consecutive payments for the statement balance in full. Once any residual interest has been paid, no further interest will be charged.

As you were not paying the statement balance in full I request you to make the payments for 2 consecutive statements I request you to make the payment of the last statement balance and current statement balance in full I request you to make the payment {$4300.00} therefore you wont be charged any interest further on your remaining balance '' I told her this was confusing with her earlier request that I make " two consecutive payments, '' and got this response : " I requested you to make the payment for the current statement which is your current balance. '' When I reminded her she previously spoke of " two consecutive payments, '' she just responded, " You need to pay the amount in full. '' She never explained what she meant when she earlier said " two consecutive payments. '' She ultimately said, " Consecutive payments for interest charges on a credit card can refer to the interest that builds up on an unpaid balance over multiple billing cycles. '' She never suggested an amount to avoid or lower the fees or what amount to pay, other than repeated requests to pay the balance to avoid further charges, which I obviously understand how credit cards work.

She did not explain why I had to make " two consecutive payments. '' I told her I have not made new charges and am trying to pay it off. I don't want to cancel the card because that affects my credit score. I'm trying to do the right thing. But the interest and fees charged AFTER I make the early payment and after other interest and fees are assessed is eating most of the payments.

I asked to receive a transcript of the chat. XXXX told me there is a " plus '' sign on the side of the chat window. There was no such sign. She told me I could " take a screenshot of the conversation. '' So I did that, if you need it.

I was referred to a team for a hardship program. I had called that program before but was denied eligibility. But will call again.

To recap : I'm making the payments before the due date, which I've read helps avoid significantly more interest and fees. I realize fees and interest continue to be assessed. I'm doing this with other credit cards, and my payments are significantly reducing my balance. Citibank is the only card where I have this problem.

I'm further concerned that my interaction with customer service will " flag '' my account and subject it to cancellation. I'm trying to do the right thing and pay the card off. I don't want to cancel it, and I don't want it cancelled, because that affects my credit score. But the high fees and interest assessed even after I make early payments are preventing that.

I'm also concerned that making this report to you will " flag '' my account for cancellation by Citibank. I hope you have protections in place in case they take retributive action like this.

I am an educated person. I realize I got myself in this situation by running up the credit card debt with a high APR. However, the interest and fees which are tagged on AFTER I make more than the minimum payment are significantly impacting my effort to pay the card off. Ironically, the card statement shows if I make a certain amount of payment I can pay the card off in three years. However, that math is not correct if the interest and fees are added, so the statement is misleading, at best.

An offer by law Offer is part of contract negotiations where a party agrees to do or not do something in exchange for consideration. An offer must be stated and delivered in a way that would lead a reasonable person to expect a binding contract to arise from its acceptance. An offer gives the offeree the ability to accept and form an enforceable contract. 

When a valid offer is made, an acceptance by the offeree creates a binding contract. An offeror generally can not retract the offer once the other party has accepted. A court may not find a binding contract regardless, though, if the negotiation did not involve consideration, involves an illusory promise, or if the offeror did not have the capacity to enter into the contract. However, a contract offer can be withdrawn by notification to the offeree of the intent to withdraw the offer before the offeree has accepted. Offerors typically can withdraw an offer before acceptance in any contract negotiation unless the parties have created an enforceable option contract. If the offeree rejects the offer, the offer can no longer be accepted by the offeree. 

An offer can also be made in the form of a counteroffer. The offeree that receives the initial offer can make a new offer of their own instead of accepting the initial offer. This counteroffer acts as a rejection of the initial offer and creates an entirely new offer that can be accepted or rejected. 

Consideration is a promise, performance, or forbearance bargained by a promisor in exchange for their promise. Consideration is the main element of a contract. Without consideration by both parties, a contract can not be enforceable. For instance, if a person used the money to purchase an apple, the apple is the merchants consideration, and the money is the persons consideration. 

Types : Consideration could be a promise, performance, forbearance, or property with legal value, but the economic benefit is not required. 
A gift or gratuitous promise can not be a consideration for they have no bargaining. The past performance also can not be a consideration as there is no exchange. 

Substitute for consideration : A contract without consideration could be enforceable if it has a substitute. Substitutes are promissory estoppel or detrimental reliance under Restatement ( Second ) of Contracts, or good faith modification under UCC. 
Promissory estoppel/detrimental reliance : A contract without consideration is enforceable if the nonperformance of the promisor will cause injustice. Elements of promissory estoppel are ( i ) the promise has reasonable, foreseeable, and detrimental reliance on the promisor, and ( ii ) the enforcement of the promise is necessary to avoid injustice. 
Good faith modification : A modified contract is a kind of new agreement, which changes parties obligations and then requires new consideration. But contract modification made in good faith under UCC is enforceable even without consideration
